data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ilyssa' has a rich cultural history, with its roots in ancient Greece. It was believed that Ilyssa was a powerful nymph or goddess who inhabited the sea and managed its ebb and flow. This associations lends an air of mystery and enchantment to the name. Ilyssa has been featured in literature, art, and song throughout history. It has also been a popular name among Christians, who may see her as a symbol of divine protection and guidance, much like other sea deities such as St. Ursula or St. Catherine of Alexandria.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Ilyssa' holds deep spiritual significance, as it connects us to the divine power and majesty of the ocean, a prime symbol of God's creation and sustenance. By invoking the name 'Ilyssa', we are reminded of the flowing, endless nature of God's love and mercy, and the power of the Holy Spirit to guide us through uncharted waters and into new realms of faith and understanding. The name also invokes the spiritual qualities of beauty, grace, and mystery, reminding us of the hidden depths of God's divine nature and ancient wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ilyssa is mentioned in the works of the Byzantine historian Procopius as a name of a noblewoman. The name Ilyssa carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Ilyssa is associated with the aristocracy of the Byzantine Empire during the reign of Emperor Justinian I.
